haiku-low.q1: If reports.row_count is 10,000 or less, the CSV is returned directly (200, text/csv). If it is above 10,000, NULL or missing, or the row cap of 10,001 rows is hit, a background job runs and the user gets 202 JSON with the export state.
haiku-low.q2: The POST returns the active export as 200 JSON with already_active true, showing its own filters. No new export is created, and the user must wait until it is done or failed, then click again.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link is a signed URL valid for 86,400 seconds (24 hours). The existing 7-day bucket lifecycle rule deletes the stored file. The page's Download endpoint can issue a new link until expiry.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, with 60 s and 300 s backoff. After the third failure the row is marked failed with a user-safe error, an export_failed email is sent, and the page shows Failed with that error.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read from the read replica only. Export state and the exports table are read from the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: In the exports table in the primary database. The page calls the status GET on load and polls every 5 s while queued or running. Reopening the page shows the user's most recent export.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica, encodes them to CSV, and uploads 8 MiB multipart parts as it goes. Memory stays at one buffer and one page, not growing with row count. Peak memory is still to be measured.
haiku-low.q8: Uploaded parts stay in an invisible incomplete multipart upload, aborted on handled errors and discarded by the bucket after 24 hours. Nothing is downloadable. The next attempt starts from scratch with a new upload to the same key.
haiku-low.q9: Stored as text in the exports row's filters and cols columns, saved after validation. The job receives only the export_id in its payload and re-parses the stored values with build_rows_query.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The INSERT uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so the database lets only one request create the active export.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be complete and the row marked done. The job then creates a 24-hour signed URL, sends export_ready, and sets email_sent_at. A rerun on a finished export with email_sent_at set does nothing; without it, it only resends the email.
haiku-low.q12: The whole CSV is built in memory before any response, so a failure returns 500 with no file and nothing to clean up. Exceeding 45 s returns 503. The user can click again.

sonnet.q1: POST endpoint reads reports.row_count. 10,000 rows or fewer: builds the CSV and returns it directly (200, text/csv), no job or storage. More than 10,000, NULL or missing: records an export row, enqueues a background job, returns 202 JSON describing the export (status queued); the job writes the CSV to the exports bucket and emails a 24-hour link. If a small-path read hits 10,001 rows (stale row_count), it discards the CSV and switches to the large path.
sonnet.q2: No second export is created. The endpoint returns the already-active export as HTTP 200 JSON with already_active: true, carrying that export's own filters and cols. The page shows 'Export in progress for: <filters>' plus the state label and polls. If the new click had different filters, the user gets no CSV for the new view and must wait until the active export is done or failed, then click again.
sonnet.q3: The emailed signed link lasts 24 hours (86,400 s, the maximum), generated when the email is sent. The existing 7-day lifecycle rule on the exports bucket deletes the file (7 days after creation). The page marks it expired when finished_at is older than 7 days.
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts, with 60 s then 300 s backoff. After the third failure the queue calls on_final_failure once: the row is set to failed with a short user-safe error and finished_at, and an export_failed email is sent. The page shows 'Failed' followed by the error text, and the user can click Download CSV again. (Exception: if the row is already done, it is not marked failed; only an error log is written and the page still shows done with a Download button.) No file is downloadable.
sonnet.q5: Report rows (report_rows) are read only from the read replica for both the small and large paths. The export status row and reports.row_count/metadata are read from the primary (which database holds the reports table is not stated).
sonnet.q6: Status is stored in the new exports table (status column: queued, running, done, failed) in the primary database. The page's export panel calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/export on page load, which returns the user's most recent export (read from the primary), so a returning user sees the state. It also uses the POST response for the first render and polls that GET every 5 s while the state is queued or running, stopping on done or failed.
sonnet.q7: It streams the CSV into a multipart upload. It reads 5,000-row pages from the read replica by keyset, encodes them into an in-memory buffer, and uploads a part whenever the buffer reaches 8 MiB, then empties the buffer. Memory stays at one 8 MiB buffer, one page of rows and a list of at most ~113 etags, so it does not grow with report size. complete_multipart then publishes the file. The job sets a ~1500 s deadline within the 1800 s attempt limit.
sonnet.q8: Nothing partial is ever visible, because the object only appears at complete_multipart. On an error the except block calls abort_multipart (best effort) and re-raises. If the worker is killed, the orphaned upload is invisible and the bucket's 24-hour rule discards it. The queue keeps no progress, so the next attempt starts from scratch: a new multipart upload and the header and first page again, using the same deterministic key.
sonnet.q9: They are saved as text columns (filters and cols) on the exports row, as the strings from the page URL, after validation in Step 2. The enqueue payload holds only the export_id (payload limit 64 KB), and the job loads the row and re-parses them with build_rows_query.
sonnet.q10: A partial unique index on exports (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running'), in the database. The insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING *; the request that gets no row back selects the active export and returns it with already_active: true.
sonnet.q11: The file must have been completed (complete_multipart) and the row marked status done with object_key, rows_written and finished_at; then a signed URL is generated and send_email sent, and email_sent_at set. On a re-run: if the row is failed, return doing nothing; if done and email_sent_at is set, return (duplicate delivery); if done without email_sent_at, skip the rebuild and go straight to the email step. Otherwise a conditional claim UPDATE (attempt < ctx.attempt) lets only one copy proceed. Duplicate emails are possible in rare cases and accepted.
sonnet.q12: The whole CSV is built in memory before anything is sent, so a failure gives a clean error and no truncated file. A replica error returns 500. If more than 45 s elapse (checked between pages) it returns 503. Nothing was created, so nothing needs cleanup, and the page shows 'Export failed, try again.' and the user can click again.
